content.thinking:
I'm checking the claims against the cause. The cause names account page requests failing, but the 27.2% average means not every request did, so I can't say all shoppers who opened those pages were affected.

I'm weighing whether the claim that account pages failed for every shopper who opened them holds up, since the error rates only reach 40.5% at peak and never show every request failing. I'm treating the monthly-spending trigger as supported, because the plain-words explanation states it without hedging, and I'm checking the worst-minute and takings figures against their sources.

I'm going through the remaining claims about the feature flag revert and the demo user who closed the incident before Argus checked the revert. Both line up with the timeline entries, and I'm noting that the demo user also recorded keeping the flag off and telling the checkout team.

content.text: I found one problem: the overview's first sentence says the account pages failed for every shopper who opened them, but the record shows that at most 40.5% of account page requests failed. Every other claim matches the record.

flags.quote: On io-shop, account pages failed for shoppers who opened them for {duration}.
flags.why: The record shows only some account page requests failed, at most 40.5% in any minute, but this says the pages failed for every shopper who opened them.
